Following Gabel’s arrival, Lützow convened a council of war at Gjellebekk, where it was resolved to retake Moss. Brigadier Vincents Budde was entrusted with command of the operation and devised a coordinated two-pronged assault. He would advance from the south with 1,000 men of the 2nd Trondheim Regiment. At the same time, Lieutenant Colonel Henrik Jørgen Huitfeldt would land north of the town with 560 soldiers from the Smaalenske Regiment, cutting off Falkenberg’s line of retreat.
BATTLE SECTION
The battle was concluded by 09:00 when Falkenberg was mortally wounded and forced to capitulate. Norwegian forces inflicted heavy losses; around 100 Swedes were killed and more than 532 captured; by contrast, their own casualties were comparatively light, some 30 killed and 86 wounded. Subsequently, the defense of the town was entrusted to 800 infantry, 400 armed peasants, and 3 dragoon companies.
